Observed on one node on v0.14.0: 335 streams held in one team project, 4,155 asks, 12,994 declines, and about 1,000 fresh asks in a burst at each upgrade, because an upgrade clears every give-up. Present since v0.11.0.\\n\\nThe gate is \\u0060RunLauncher.EnsurePrReviewPreflightSafeAsync\\u0060; \\u0060PrReviewPreflightCompleted\\u0060 has no entry in \\u0060TaskActClassificationRegistry\\u0060. Today the hold is accidentally the only thing keeping another owner\\u0027s verdict out of that gate, so the genesis entry must never ship without the owner check. pull-request review pre-flight stays on the node that ran it: its events do not replicate, a node neither applies nor holds one from a peer, and the records already held leave the held table on their own with no catch-up traffic.\u0022},\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:[\u0022A node that runs a pre-flight puts none of its dispatched, completed, abandoned or reclaimed events in its outbox, and a catch-up request for that stream is answered as nothing held here.\u0022,\u0022A pre-flight event of any of those four types delivered by a peer is neither applied nor held, on a node that has never seen the stream and on the node that dispatched it: that node\\u0027s pre-flight document is unchanged and the held table gains no row.\u0022,\u0022On a build with this fix, the first sweep of a project removes every held pre-flight record and mints no catch-up ask for one, and \\u0060h9k status\\u0060 no longer counts those streams as held or given up. A held record of any other event type is untouched, with its ask count and give-up mark intact.\u0022,\u0022A node claiming a pr-review task whose only verdict was reached on another node runs its own pre-flight before any checkout, for an ordinary review dispatch and for a mention follow-up.\u0022,\u0022A test fails if a \\u0060ReplicationStreamFamily\\u0060 value has no stream-starting event named in \\u0060AggregateGenesisEventTypes\\u0060 and is not on an explicit exemption list.\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022Pre-flight events are classified project-scoped (\\u0060EventScopeRegistry.cs:409-416\\u0060) so that a fleet sibling reclaiming a task could read the verdict, but \\u0060PrReviewPreflightDispatched\\u0060 was never added to \\u0060AggregateGenesisEventTypes.IsGenesis\\u0060, so every receiver has held them since v0.11.0 (\\u0060EventReplicationInbox.cs:1376\\u0060) and no node has ever read another node\\u0027s verdict. The held-tail sweep then asks the fleet for a record it already has. Observed on one node on v0.14.0: 335 streams held in one team project, 4,155 asks, 12,994 declines, and about 1,000 fresh asks at each upgrade, because an upgrade clears every give-up (\\u0060EventCatchUpCoordinator.cs:500-522\\u0060).\\n\\nThis change ratifies what has shipped. Classify the four events NodeScoped, the same shape as the courier\\u0027s events (\\u0060EventScopeRegistry.cs:394-396\\u0060). The outbox, \\u0060EventCatchUpResponder\\u0060 and \\u0060EventReplicationInbox.ApplyAsync\\u0060 (\\u0060:799\\u0060) already act on that classification, so no new check is needed and the pre-flight gate in \\u0060RunLauncher\\u0060 does not change. \\u0060TaskRequeued\\u0060 and \\u0060PrReviewPreflightParked\\u0060 stay on the task stream and keep travelling.\\n\\nClear held pre-flight records at the top of \\u0060RequestHeldTailStreamsAsync\\u0060, ahead of the give-up reset, so the upgrade never mints the burst. \\u0060HeldReplicatedEventRecord\\u0060 has no type column, so use one delete keyed on the event type inside \\u0060RecordJson\\u0060 rather than reading full documents every sweep (commit 1e4c9a82c removed that cost). Nothing is lost: each origin keeps its own log and no reader needs a peer\\u0027s copy.\\n\\nRemove what this leaves unreachable: the pre-flight branch in \\u0060ReplicationProjectResolver\\u0060, \\u0060ReplicationStreamFamily.PrReviewPreflight\\u0060, and its \\u0060FamilyOf\\u0060 arm. Rewrite the comments that say verdicts travel or that nodes share a database (\\u0060EventScopeRegistry.cs:398-422\\u0060, \\u0060RunLauncher.cs:2235-2241\\u0060).\\n\\nDuring rollout a peer on v0.14.0 keeps sending these events; a fixed node refuses each with a warning at \\u0060:799\\u0060 and holds nothing, which is expected. Tests fit the existing setup: \\u0060EventCatchUpTests\\u0060 (\\u0060InMemoryMessageTransport\\u0060, \\u0060FakeLedger\\u0060) and \\u0060RunLauncherTests\\u0060. Describe this pull request as the behaviour change
